confirmed.title: Moving a case (or reflection or note) to the recycle bin takes two separate writes up to 3 s apart. If the app dies between them, the case still exists on the server but every device hides it for 30+ days, and Restore cannot bring it back
confirmed.scenario:
1. A resident in theatre with no signal opens a case and taps Delete (edit page), deletes several from the Logbook list, or uses Undo while typing the next case. All of these call moveToBin.
2. moveToBin first awaits cloud.saveBinEntry (bin.js:55). That goes through queued(), which offline waits the full ACK_WAIT of 3 s (cloud.js:110). The bin entry goes into Firestore's persistent queue at 0 ms. Because the tomb feed applies pending local bin entries at once, the case vanishes from the list immediately.
3. Only after that wait does removeCase put the delete in the write queue (bin.js:68 to writes.save to the recovery store).
4. Within those 3 s the resident pockets the phone or swipes the app away. iOS suspends the PWA and later ends it (or Android kills it, or another tab's 'Reload' fires controllerchange and reloads every tab). The delete job is never created.
5. At the next start Firestore sends the queued bin entry, and settleLate restamps it, so every device sees it. No delete exists.
confirmed.consequence: The case stays on the server, so it is still counted in the owner's reads and the drift check. The bin entry's tombstone (binTombs uses the binned version's updatedAt, applyTombs) hides it on every device. This includes fresh devices and weekly full reads, because the bin feed re-applies the tombstone. It lasts as long as the bin entry exists (30 days). After the purge and the next full read, the 'deleted' case comes back: the #519 zombie symptom by another route. Meanwhile the header says '✓ Synced' and the in-app counts and summaries leave the case out. Restore from the bin does not help: the restore write equals the server copy apart from updatedAt, so checkWrite makes no write and the server stamp stays old. gone[id] then keeps hiding the case once the synced job leaves the overlay. Reflections (bin entry, then a direct deleteReflection) and notes split the same way.
confirmed.fix: Make the bin copy and the delete one atomic write. Carry the bin entry on the delete job (e.g. writes.save('case', owner, { id, _deleted: true, _bin: entry }, base)). In commitRecord's transaction, after compare() passes, do tx.set(binRef, entry) followed by tx.delete(ref). A conflict then writes neither, so rollBack is not needed for cases and notes. For reflections, put the bin set and the deleteDoc in one writeBatch. As a cheaper stop-gap, persist the delete job before awaiting saveBinEntry. Either way, add a start-up check: a bin entry whose record still exists at the binned version and has no pending delete job should get its delete finished, or the entry removed.
verifier_fix:
The direction is right (make the bin copy and the delete atomic), with four corrections:

1. Cases and notes: if the bin entry is written inside commitRecord's transaction, stamp its deletedAt when the transaction commits, not at the time of the tap. Delete jobs can run hours later when signal returns. Other devices only read bin entries with deletedAt after their last sync minus SKEW, and a transaction write gets no restampIfLate.
2. Reflections: put the bin set and the deleteDoc in one writeBatch. Keep it going through queued() with late(email, 'bin', [id], 'deletedAt') so it is still restamped.
3. Do not use the suggested stop-gap of saving the delete job before saveBinEntry. If the page dies between the two it reverses the failure: the original is deleted with no bin copy, which is real data loss. A safer stop-gap: call setDoc for the bin entry, wait only for its local write (a few ms), not the 3 s ACK_WAIT, then save the delete job straight away.
4. Start-up check: only after a server-confirmed read, a bin entry whose original still exists with the same signature as e.data, and with no pending job for that record, gets a delete job with base = e.data. Note separately that on full reads replaceAll ignores meta.gone, which makes hiding depend on snapshot order.

confirmed.title: Pasted-list save is not crash-safe: the response-sheet entries are queued only after a wait of up to 3 s, and the list's case ids are not kept. A kill in that window drops the sheet rows, and saving the still-present list again duplicates every case
confirmed.scenario:
1. A programme resident (sheet outbox on) pastes an OT list offline, taps Review, then Save.
2. ui-log.js:1203 creates new uids for the cases. saveMany adds them to the list at once (applyLocal), then awaits cloud.saveCases (ui-core.js:495). Offline, queued() waits the full ACK_WAIT of 3 s.
3. toSheet(cases) runs only after that (ui-core.js:496). The box is cleared (ui-log.js:1212) only after it too.
4. The resident locks the phone or swipes the app away within those seconds. iOS ends the suspended app, or Android kills it, or a service-worker 'Reload' in another tab reloads this one.
5. At the next start the cases batch, already in Firestore's persistent queue, syncs. No sheetOutbox entries were ever written. The pasted text is still in the box in List mode (the draft was saved on input and on pagehide).
6. Thinking the save failed, the resident taps Review and Save again. New uids are minted and there is no duplicate check for pasted lists, so every case is saved twice. Only the second copies go to the sheet.
confirmed.consequence: The response sheet is missing the whole first list (the Case tab, Database and AY Totals undercount), with no catch-up. If the list is saved again, the app holds every case twice, which inflates the counts towards targets, while the sheet holds them once. Single cases have the same gap but shorter (about 180 ms, createCase ui-core.js:447 runs toSheet after writes.save). Those are protected against duplicates by draft.caseId; pasted lists have no such id.
confirmed.fix: Queue the sheet entries no later than the cases. Either call toSheet(cases) before `await cloud.saveCases` (Firestore sends queued writes in order), or add the sheetOutbox sets to the same batch as the cases in saveCases when `sheet` is set; the ids are fresh, so a create-only rule cannot refuse them. For single cases, carry the outbox entry on the case's queue job and write it in commitRecord's transaction when the case does not exist yet. Also mint the pasted cases' ids at Review and keep them in the draft (like draft.caseId), so a save repeated after a crash rewrites the same ids instead of duplicating them.
verifier_fix:
Queue the sheet entries as soon as the batch has been handed to Firestore, not when it is acknowledged. Do not put them in the cases' own batch or transaction. If they share a batch or transaction, a rules refusal of an outbox entry (validOutbox, or the rid get() against logbooks/me differing from the client's view) fails the whole batch, and the cases are lost. That breaks the "never a reason for a save to fail" design at ui-core.js:451.

Concretely, in saveMany: `const p = cloud.saveCases(mine(), cases); if (sheet) toSheet(cases); await p;`. Both functions first await sdk(), so the batch commit is issued before the outbox setDocs. Both then sit in Firestore's persistent mutation queue within milliseconds, in order. For a list over BATCH (450 cases), queue each part's outbox entries right after that part's commit.

Apply the same idea to createCase: call toSheet once writes.save has persisted the job, rather than after its 180 ms race. The case id is fresh, so the outbox create cannot conflict.

For the duplicates: mint ids at Review, store them in the draft next to bulkText (draft.bulkIds, like draft.caseId), and reuse them on Save. A re-save after a crash then rewrites the same docs, and the create-only outbox rule refuses the repeat entries harmlessly. Also add the single-case twin check (same date and normalised text) to saveBulk and to the plan 'Done' path, which have the same re-tap duplication.

confirmed.title: Two windows of the app on one device do not share the save queue: a save left by a closed window is never sent by the window still open, which says '✓ Synced'. A late duplicate drain records a false conflict that blocks later saves of that case
confirmed.scenario:
(a) A resident has the installed app open, plus a browser tab of the logbook (Android, or a laptop). In the tab they save or edit a case while the Wi-Fi is flaky, or close the tab right after Save: writes.save returns after 180 ms, before the transaction commits. The job sits 'pending' in the shared recovery store. The installed app's queue only knows the jobs it listed at activate(). kick() (writes.js:66), called on 'online', drains only those. So it never sends the job, and its header says '✓ Synced' (writes.pending() is 0). The case's sheetOutbox entry, which went to Firestore's shared queue, does reach the response sheet. The case reaches the server only when some page is next loaded. If the resident meanwhile logs it again on the phone because it is 'missing', it is duplicated once the job drains.
(b) A case edit is left pending, and two windows then start and both list that job. The foreground window sends it and the case is edited again (v2). The background window was frozen or throttled; when it wakes, it drains its stale copy (base v0, record v1). It gets a conflict and persists state 'conflict' over the 'synced' state the other window saved.
confirmed.consequence: (a) The header shows 'Synced' while a case is not on the server, for as long as the other window stays open (days for an installed app). The response sheet can briefly hold a case the server does not have, and a re-log causes duplicates. (b) From then on every start shows 'Save needs attention', and every later save of that case waits behind the stale conflict and never syncs until it is resolved in Recent changes. There, 'Restore my version' would put back the older v1 text over v2.
confirmed.fix: Treat the recovery store as shared. On a BroadcastChannel ping after every put, and on 'online' and visibilitychange to visible, re-list store.list(owner) and merge in jobs this tab has not seen. Before draining a job, re-read its persisted record: if another tab has already settled it (synced or archived), adopt that state and do not send. Never let persist() overwrite a terminal persisted state with a non-terminal copy. Alternatively, drain under navigator.locks.request('apmes-logbook-writes:'+email), re-listing inside the lock. Optionally warn on beforeunload while writes.pending() > 0.

confirmed.title: A resident added to the programme list after they started using the app is recognised mid-session, but their logbook never gets its rid in that session, so none of that session's cases go to the response sheet
confirmed.scenario:
1. A resident signs in to the logbook before an admin has put them on the residents list (common for new intakes, SMOs, or an email fixed on the list later). That start caches who = { resident: null } in localStorage (saveWho).
2. The admin adds them in People.
3. Next app start: onUser uses the cached `known` who, so S.resident is null and the rid save at app.js:1016 (`if (resident && logbook.rid !== resident.rid) cloud.saveLogbook(...)`) is skipped.
4. refreshWho (app.js:930) gets the server's answer and sets S.resident (app.js:935). It reloads the logbook, which still has no rid, and never saves the rid.
5. Every case logged until the next page load reaches createCase or saveMany, and toSheet's guard (ui-core.js:454 `S.resident && S.logbook?.rid === S.resident.rid`) is false. The rules would refuse the entry anyway, since sheetOutbox create needs logbooks/{me}.rid.
confirmed.consequence: All of that session's new app cases, which can span days for an installed app left open, are missing from the response sheet's Case tab, Database and AY Totals for good. Nothing re-sends them, and the sheet then undercounts against the app. The same session's summary writes for Programme totals also go out without the logbook rid.
confirmed.fix: In refreshWho, when w.resident is set and (S.logbook.rid || null) !== w.resident.rid, queue cloud.saveLogbook(email, { rid }) and set S.logbook.rid locally. In the start path, after queueing the rid save, also set S.logbook.rid = resident.rid, so the outbox works right away and a cached logbook does not hide it. Optionally, at start, re-queue outbox entries for the resident's recent source app/paste cases created since their rid was saved. Because entries are create-only per case id, a re-send is refused rather than duplicated while the old entry is still waiting, though one the script has already consumed would be created again, so this catch-up needs a 'sent' marker.
verifier_fix:
Use one helper for both places, for example `ensureRid(user)`: `if (S.resident && S.logbook && S.logbook.rid !== S.resident.rid) { S.logbook.rid = S.resident.rid; cloud.saveLogbook(user.email, { rid: S.resident.rid }).catch(() => {}); }`.

Call it where app.js:1016 is now. In refreshWho, call it only after the `S.logbook = lb` replacement and adoptShared step. If it ran earlier, it would change the logbook before the `S.logbook === firstLogbook` check, and it would also be overwritten by the server copy that has no rid.

Leave out the optional catch-up re-queue. The plan says the outbox does no back-fill, a re-send would need a new 'sent' marker to avoid making Case rows twice, and the drift check already reports the missed cases.
